input.strategy_title: Integrated GenAI model evaluation for RHOAI
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Customers adopting generative models on RHOAI have no supported way to answer
"is this model good enough for my use case?" inside the platform. Evaluation
today happens in ad-hoc notebooks with lm-evaluation-harness or vendor tools,
results live in spreadsheets, and nothing links an evaluation to the model
version that was actually deployed. We need a first-class evaluation capability:
run standard and custom benchmarks against models served on the platform,
persist results alongside the model version, and let users compare candidates
before promoting one to production.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1  | P0 | Users can launch an evaluation of a model served on the platform (KServe endpoint or Llama Stack distribution) against a selected benchmark suite. |
| HLR-2  | P0 | Standard benchmark suites (e.g. MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag exposed through lm-eval task names) are available out of the box. |
| HLR-3  | P0 | Evaluation results are persisted and linked to the Model Registry version of the evaluated model. |
| HLR-4  | P1 | Users can define custom evaluation tasks (own datasets and metrics) and run them through the same flow. |
| HLR-5  | P1 | The Dashboard shows evaluation runs, their status, and per-benchmark scores, and allows side-by-side comparison of two model versions. |
| HLR-6  | P1 | Evaluations can be embedded as a step in a Data Science Pipeline so promotion flows can gate on scores. |
| HLR-7  | P1 | Llama Stack's eval provider API is backed by the platform evaluation service, so agents/apps built on Llama Stack get the same results. |
| HLR-8  | P2 | Evaluation runs record cost/duration metadata (tokens, wall-clock, GPU time) for capacity planning. |
| HLR-9  | P2 | Product documentation covers the evaluation workflow end to end, including custom task authoring. |

## Affected Components

- TrustyAI
- Llama Stack
- Dashboard
- Data Science Pipelines
- Model Registry

## Out of Scope

- Human-preference (arena style) evaluation collection
- Automatic model promotion decisions — pipelines gate, humans promote
- Fine-tuning feedback loops driven by evaluation scores

## Open Questions

1. Execution engine: TrustyAI's LMEvalJob (Tech Preview) already wraps
   lm-evaluation-harness — do we build on it as the single execution path, or is
   a new evaluation service needed to also serve Llama Stack's eval provider
   API? Needs a technical investigation with a recommendation.
2. Result schema: what is the canonical result format persisted to Model
   Registry custom properties, and does it survive benchmark-suite version
   bumps? Prototype against real MMLU output before committing.
3. Benchmark dataset licensing: which standard suites can we redistribute in
   disconnected environments, and which must be fetched by the customer?

# Extend TrustyAI LMEvalJob as the single evaluation execution path

## Description

Branch A of the execution-engine decision: build on TrustyAI's LMEvalJob (the
platform's existing lm-evaluation-harness wrapper, currently Tech Preview) as
the single execution path for GenAI model evaluation. Users can launch an
evaluation of a model served on the platform — a KServe endpoint or a Llama
Stack distribution — against a selected benchmark suite, including custom
evaluation tasks, with results emitted in the canonical result schema.

## Scope

- Extend the LMEvalJob capability so an evaluation can target a model served
  on a KServe/ModelMesh inference endpoint or on a Llama Stack distribution
  (LlamaStackDistribution), not just the job's current target surface.
- Support user-defined custom evaluation tasks (own datasets and metrics)
  running through the same job flow as standard lm-eval task names.
- Emit evaluation results in the canonical result schema (per-benchmark
  scores, suite name and version, evaluated model version linkage) and persist
  them to Model Registry linked to the evaluated model version.
- Record cost/duration metadata (tokens, wall-clock, GPU time) on evaluation
  runs for capacity planning.
- Job lifecycle and status reporting sufficient for the Dashboard's run list
  and status views (running, succeeded, failed) and for pipeline-step
  consumption.
- Address Tech Preview maturity gaps identified by the execution-engine
  decision for the capabilities this path now carries.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Given** a model served on a KServe endpoint and a selected standard
  benchmark suite, **when** an evaluation is launched, **then** the job runs to
  completion against that endpoint and records per-benchmark scores, measured
  by a completed run with retrievable results.
- **Given** a model served via a Llama Stack distribution, **when** an
  evaluation is launched, **then** the same flow completes against the
  distribution's endpoint, measured by a completed run.
- **Given** a user-defined custom task (own dataset and metric), **when** it is
  submitted through the evaluation flow, **then** it runs and scores like a
  standard suite, measured by a custom-task run with persisted results.
- **Given** a completed evaluation, **when** results are persisted, **then**
  they follow the canonical result schema and are linked to the evaluated
  model's Model Registry version, measured by retrieval from Model Registry.
- Evaluation runs record tokens, wall-clock, and GPU time metadata.
- Run status is observable throughout the job lifecycle.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): launch an evaluation of a served model against a selected
  benchmark suite — full coverage for branch A.
- HLR-4 (P1): custom evaluation tasks through the same flow — full coverage.
- HLR-8 (P2): cost/duration metadata recorded by evaluation runs — full
  coverage.
- HLR-3 (P0, writer side): this epic emits and persists the results that the
  Model Registry persistence capability stores.

## Dependencies (plain terms)

Exists only if the execution-engine decision selects extending LMEvalJob.
Depends on that decision and on the evaluation result persistence and model
version linking capability: the job code emits and persists results through
that capability's canonical-schema linking surface, which is itself gated by
the canonical result schema prototype — a schema revision rewrites this epic's
emission implementation just as it rewrites the persistence implementation. If
the decision instead recommends a new evaluation service, this epic is dropped
in favor of the new-service branch.

# Llama Stack eval provider backed by the TrustyAI execution path

## Description

Branch A of the execution-engine decision: implement Llama Stack's eval
provider API as a provider backed by the platform's evaluation capability
delivered through the extended TrustyAI LMEvalJob execution path, so agents and
apps built on Llama Stack get the same evaluation results as the platform flow.

## Scope

- Implement an eval provider for Llama Stack (provider-plugin model, configured
  per LlamaStackDistribution) that delegates evaluations to the TrustyAI
  execution path.
- Map the Llama Stack eval provider API operations onto the platform
  evaluation flow (launch evaluation against a served model, retrieve status
  and scores).
- Wire the provider as the production eval provider in the platform's Llama
  Stack distribution, replacing the current state where the eval provider API
  exists upstream but no production eval provider is wired in the platform
  distribution.
- Return results consistent with the canonical result schema so Llama
  Stack-based consumers see the same scores as the Dashboard and pipeline
  flows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Given** a LlamaStackDistribution with the platform eval provider
  configured, **when** an agent or app calls the Llama Stack eval provider
  API, **then** an evaluation is launched through the platform execution path
  and results are returned, measured by an API-level test against a served
  model.
- **Given** the same model and suite evaluated via the platform flow and via
  the Llama Stack eval provider API, **then** the per-benchmark scores agree,
  measured by a comparison test.
- The provider is wired into the platform Llama Stack distribution
  configuration as the production eval provider.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-7 (P1): Llama Stack's eval provider API backed by the platform
  evaluation service — full coverage for branch A.

## Dependencies (plain terms)

Exists only if the execution-engine decision selects extending LMEvalJob.
Depends on that decision and on the extended TrustyAI LMEvalJob execution
capability it builds against (framework before consumer). If the decision
instead recommends a new evaluation service, this epic is dropped in favor of
the new-service provider wiring.

# License validation for the new evaluation service dependencies

## Description

Branch B of the execution-engine decision: run license scanning and validation
for the new evaluation service's dependency tree before the service
implementation commits to its dependencies. The service wraps
lm-evaluation-harness and serves the platform evaluation API, so its transitive
dependency set must be license-clean for redistribution.

## Scope

- Run license scanning over the new evaluation service's planned dependency
  set (lm-evaluation-harness and its transitive dependencies, serving/API
  frameworks identified by the execution-engine decision).
- Classify findings: approved licenses, problematic licenses requiring
  substitution or exclusion, and items needing legal review.
- Produce remediation decisions for problematic dependencies (alternative
  library, isolation, or exclusion) so the service implementation starts from
  a validated dependency list.
- Record the validated dependency baseline for later re-scans.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The planned dependency tree is scanned and every finding is classified
  (approved / remediate / legal review).
- Problematic dependencies have a documented remediation decision.
- The service implementation can start from the validated dependency baseline
  without re-running the analysis, measured by hand-off of the baseline.

- Enabling work for HLR-1 (P0): protects the new evaluation service that
  delivers HLR-1 from licensing failures. No direct HLR coverage.

## Dependencies (plain terms)

Exists only if the execution-engine decision selects building a new evaluation
service. Depends on that decision (it defines the service's dependency set);
runs in parallel with the repo onboarding. If the decision instead extends
TrustyAI's LMEvalJob, this epic is dropped.

Branch B of the execution-engine decision: implement the new evaluation
service — the platform's single execution path for GenAI model evaluation. The
service wraps lm-evaluation-harness, exposes the platform evaluation API, and
serves as the backend for Llama Stack's eval provider API. Users can launch an
evaluation of a model served on the platform (KServe endpoint or Llama Stack
distribution) against a selected benchmark suite, including custom evaluation
tasks, with results persisted per the canonical result schema.

## Scope

- Implement the evaluation service: launching evaluations of models served on
  KServe endpoints and Llama Stack distributions against selected benchmark
  suites, executing them via lm-evaluation-harness, with job lifecycle and
  status reporting.
- Expose the platform evaluation API consumed by the Dashboard, Data Science
  Pipelines, and the Llama Stack eval provider wiring.
- Support user-defined custom evaluation tasks (own datasets and metrics)
  through the same flow as standard lm-eval task names.
- Emit results in the canonical result schema and persist them to Model
  Registry linked to the evaluated model version.
- Record cost/duration metadata (tokens, wall-clock, GPU time) on evaluation
  runs for capacity planning.
- Deployment story for the service within the platform (how it is installed
  and managed per data science project), per the execution-engine decision's
